newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MAY 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MAY 9.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Single-digit interest rates on index-linked bonds on May 19. The state's new issues of bonds later this month and Treasury bills on June 2 are expected to carry interest rates of below 10.0 percent.

--New legislation submitted to Parliament will put a temporary freeze on all debts owed by ailing enterprises on the way to privatisation. The bill is expected to quickly ease the situation for Softex, Athens Paper Mills.

--Single-digit interest on new state securities signal a new era which may see the serious possibility of reducing the public debt. Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis stressed that the rate cuts were the consequence of the continuing fall in inflation.

--Unionists aligned to opposition political parties are urging the General Confederation of Workers of Greece (GSEE) to absent itself from social dialogue between unions, government and employers on changes to the job market before talks begin on May 14.

--Tenants refusing to pay rents will be evicted automatically, according to amendments to existing legislation. The changes wil do away with the need to resort to the courts, leaving landlords with the option of working with a judicial official.
--June will see the premiere of the first 10-year bond with fixed interest rates.

--Inflation last month was running at 5.9 per cent and could have been lower had Greek Radio and Television not increased its charges a whopping 33.3 per cent in April. The National Statistics Service says the result is the lowest since November 1965 - when 5.6 percent was recorded - and has hopes of 5.5 per cent in May.

--Business and public organisation officials made lightning visit to Skopje in the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia yesterday organised by the foreign ministry and FYROM's Liaison office in Athens.

--The Bank of Piraeus is slowly but surely about to sign an agreement on the purchase of Sigma Securities, according to reports. The two side are expected to close the deal next week, the two sides say.
--Cabinet yesterday said it believed the legislation governing state procurements was more than adequate and would not amend it.
--The finance ministry is expected to issue a circular to other ministries regarding the drafting of the 1998 state budget. The circular stresses the containment of spending for the next year.

--Consultants McKinsey yesterday presented their restructuring report to Olympic Airways, Greece's national carrier's, board, saying the organisation could save 25 billion drachmas in wages if it reorganised its personnel and managment structure. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
